wildlife.definition: animals and plants living naturally in the wild.
wildlife.example: Have you wrapped the parcel for the wildlife charity yet?

win.definition: to come first or succeed in a game, competition, or struggle.
win.example: Why does the tortoise win the race in the end?

wind.definition: air that is moving, especially outdoors.
wind.example: The wind howled all night, didn't it?

winding.example: What carved that winding groove across the canyon floor?

windows.definition: openings in a wall or vehicle, usually covered with glass, that let in light and let you see outside.
windows.example: Was the wind really hurling dust at the windows?

windowsill.definition: the narrow shelf at the bottom of a window.
windowsill.example: A little bird landed on the windowsill.

wing.definition: one of the parts that a bird, insect, or aircraft uses to fly, sticking out from the side of its body.
wing.example: Can you be gentle when you touch the injured wing?

winner.definition: the person or team that succeeds in a competition or contest.
winner.example: The class read every post aloud before voting for a winner.

winning.definition: succeeding in a competition, game, or contest.
winning.example: Does loyalty matter more than winning?

winter.definition: the coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.
winter.example: Could the school use less energy this winter?

winters.definition: the coldest seasons of the year, one in each year.
winters.example: A continental climate usually means hot summers and very cold winters.

wise.definition: having or showing good judgement, based on knowledge and experience.
wise.example: What a wise judge that elderly woman was!

wisely.definition: in a sensible way, using good judgement and knowledge.
wisely.example: 'When firewood is scarce, we must use it wisely,' said Grandfather.

witness.definition: a person who sees something happen, especially a crime or accident, and can describe it.
witness.example: Why was the trader so furious when the witness spoke the truth?

wizard.definition: in stories, a man who has magic powers.
wizard.example: The clumsy wizard in the tale was cheerfully incompetent at simple spells.

woke.definition: stopped sleeping and became awake, in the past.
woke.example: Amal woke early to watch the sunrise over the hills.

wolf.definition: a wild animal like a large dog that hunts in groups.
wolf.example: A lonely wolf howled somewhere in the distant hills.

woman.example: What a kind woman his wife is!

won.definition: succeeded in a competition or contest, in the past.
won.example: What a powerful line, saying an idea was won without war!

won't.example: We'll be ready in five minutes, won't we?

wooden.example: Sami wrote his notes on a wooden clipboard.

woodland.definition: An area of land covered with trees and plants.
woodland.example: Which woodland creatures come out only after dark?

wool.definition: the soft, thick hair of sheep, used to make clothing and other items.
wool.example: Which textile keeps you warmest in winter, wool or fleece?

words.definition: single units of language that have meaning, spoken or written.
words.example: One single picture can say more than many words.

wore.definition: had something on your body as clothing, in the past.
wore.example: Mina wore a white dress to the celebration.

worked.definition: did a job or task, or made an effort to achieve something, in the past.
worked.example: Sami worked hard so his story would truly shine.

workers.definition: people who do a job, especially physical or manual work.
workers.example: The workers rushed to fill the empty shelves.

working.definition: doing a job or task, or the written steps that show how you solved a problem.
working.example: The characters spend the rest of the story working it out.

works.example: Emotive language works best when it is not overused.

worksheet.definition: a sheet of paper with questions or tasks for a learner to complete.
worksheet.example: Is one hour a decent amount of time to finish this worksheet?

world.definition: the Earth, along with all its countries and people.
world.example: Is a watchful parent always nearby in the animal world?

worn.definition: damaged or thin from being used a lot.
worn.example: The museum displayed crowns worn by ancient kings.

worst.definition: the least good, out of a whole group.
worst.example: A loyal friend stands beside you on your worst days, not only the best ones.

worth.definition: deserving of, or having a value equal to, something.
worth.example: Are the risks of Route B really worth saving a few hours?

woven.definition: made by crossing threads over and under each other, especially on a loom.
woven.example: 'This textile was woven by hand on a wooden loom,' said the museum guide.

wrapping.definition: paper or material used to cover something, especially a gift.
wrapping.example: Measuring each dimension of the box helped us choose the right wrapping paper.

wrinkles.definition: small folds or lines, for example in skin, cloth, or the appearance of distant hills.
wrinkles.example: From the aeroplane window, even towering mountains looked like tiny wrinkles.

wrist.definition: the joint that connects your hand to your arm.
wrist.example: The X-ray showed a small fracture in Theo's wrist after his fall.

writer.definition: a person whose job or hobby is producing books, stories, or articles.
writer.example: The writer described the setting in careful detail.

writers.definition: people whose job or hobby is producing books, stories, or articles.
writers.example: Fiction lets writers imagine worlds that do not really exist.

writing.definition: putting words down on paper or another surface, using letters.
writing.example: Maya kept leaning closer to read the faded writing.

written.definition: put down in words on paper or another surface, in the past.
written.example: Amal, have you written enough for your story?

wrong.definition: not correct or not true; mistaken.
wrong.example: Sami, you starred the wrong page by mistake!

wrote.definition: set down words on paper using a pen, pencil, or similar tool, in the past.
wrote.example: Leo wrote his memory on a strip of paper.

yawned.definition: opened your mouth wide and breathed in deeply, usually because you were tired or bored.
yawned.example: "I am too drowsy to finish this chapter tonight," yawned Nora.

yawning.definition: opening your mouth wide and breathing in deeply, usually from tiredness or boredom.
yawning.example: Did you know that yawning can seem contagious in a quiet classroom?

year.definition: the period of about 365 days that it takes the Earth to go around the sun.
year.example: Sami is now in his third year at Ehel Academy.

year's.example: Which quote from this year's stories would you share with a friend?

yearly.example: Farmers along the river valley depend on fertile soil for their yearly harvest.

years.example: Is Sami already eleven years old?

yesterday.example: Yesterday I enquired at the bookshop whether the new comics had arrived.

young.definition: having lived or existed for only a short time; not old.
young.example: Could this footprint belong to a young lemur?

younger.definition: less old than someone or something else.
younger.example: Please allow the younger children to go first!

youngest.definition: least old, out of a whole group.
youngest.example: What role did the youngest child play in the story, Amal?

youth.definition: young people generally, or the period of a person's life when they are young.
youth.example: The class made great progress on their youth charter.

zipped.definition: closed or fastened something using a zip.
zipped.example: Amal zipped her bus pass into the front pouch of her school bag.

zone.definition: an area that has a particular purpose or feature.
zone.example: What goods are produced in the industrial zone near the port?

zoo.definition: a place where wild animals are kept so that people can see them.
zoo.example: The elephant at the zoo is remarkable because it can paint pictures.

zookeeper.definition: a person whose job is looking after animals in a place where wild animals are kept for people to see.
zookeeper.example: 'Her maternal instinct told her the chick was hungry,' said the zookeeper.
